subject: TCO alignment & pilot next steps (FinLytics)
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finlytics.com>, procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>, CTO Office <cto@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: inference pilot & cost questions

Rachel — thanks for the demo and the clear breakdown. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can align on next steps: 

Quick context: FinLytics is piloting an LLM-assisted analyst feature in our core product. Current pain points we discussed:
- Peak latency spikes during monthly batch-updates (95th percentile ~1.2s) are hurting UX.
- Token spend is our top variable operating cost; at projected scale (~1.2B tokens/mo) this is material to FY28 budget.
- Need predictable unit economics for procurement sign-off; unfamiliar with how batching/caching will affect end-to-end latency.

Questions we need to resolve to move to pilot: 
1) What concrete TCO delta can we expect from batching + KV caching for our usage pattern (mix of short prompts + multi-turn context)?
2) If we commit to a 3-month dedicated pilot, what discount/commit level is reasonable and what are the guardrails?
3) What HW/config would you recommend for hits-per-second during monthly peaks (we currently provision with 4x A100s on our side)?

We're happy to share sample payloads and an anonymized traffic trace. Procurement asked that we get a pilot cost model (spreadsheet) and a short one-pager to include in the internal memo. 

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
VP Product, FinLytics
samir@finlytics.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: inference pilot & cost questions

Samir — great to meet you and the FinLytics team yesterday. Appreciate the clear framing. Below is a concise post-call recap + proposed pilot action plan so your procurement and execs have what they need. I attached a simple pilot-cost-model.xlsx and a 6-slide pilot deck (redwood-pilot-deck.pdf).

Recap of pain + goals (as I heard them):
- Pain: unpredictable per-user cost driven by token volatility and latency-related overprovisioning during monthly peaks.
- Goal: prove a 30–50% reduction in per-token spend for production inference while holding 95th-percentile latency <= 600ms during normal and <= 900ms during monthly peaks.

High-level TCO assumptions (initial, conservative):
- Current baseline: ~1.2B tokens/mo, avg request 380 tokens, 0.8M requests/mo.
- Redwood levers we expect to apply: batching (parallel request aggregation), KV/prefix caching for repetitive context, and model variant routing (quantized variant for low-latency low-cost paths).
- Modeled uplift: batching + caching -> 25–40% token-cost reduction; model routing + quantization add incremental 10–20% depending on quality tolerance.

Pilot scope (recommended):
- Duration: 8 weeks active (3 weeks ramp, 4 weeks steady-state, 1 week analysis).
- Workloads: subset of 20% of analyst queries (low-risk cohort), representative mix of short prompts (60%) and multi-turn (40%).
- Success metrics: >=25% net unit cost reduction, P95 latency <= 750ms, error/quality regressions <= 2% as measured by your prompt test set.

Operational asks from FinLytics (what we need to run the model):
- Sample payloads (anonymized) + 7-day traffic trace (for batching profile).
- A small prompt-eval set for quality regression checks (~200 examples).
- Contact for procurement to route trial commercial terms (cc'd).

Commercial framing & options: 
- Hosted pilot on Redwood Dedicated: recommend a reserved pilot pool sized to handle peak concurrency with burst headroom — we estimate 2 x high-utilization L4 instances during peak for your mix (we'll refine after we see traces).
- Typical pilot commercial: 50% discount on usage for the pilot with a commitment to a mutually-agreed throughput envelope; extension to production includes standard reserved pricing or blended commit.
- I'll follow up with a one-page commercial summary for procurement to include in the memo.

Next steps and timeline (proposed):
1) You send sample payloads + one-week traffic trace by Thu 7/1.
2) Redwood provides pilot cost model and one-page memo by Fri 7/2 (attached).
3) Technical sync with Marissa (SE) to finalize sizing — Tue 7/6 (30m).
4) Target pilot start: week of 7/12 pending procurement ok.

Marissa — adding you on the technical sizing thread; Ben is on deck for commercial. Samir/Procurement — let me know if the pilot term framing above looks acceptable.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:49:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: inference pilot & cost questions

Quick technical notes to supplement Rachel's plan — Samir, this will help you evaluate achievable latency vs savings tradeoffs.

1) Batching behavior: based on your described mix we expect mean batch sizes of 6–10 tokens-at-a-time during steady-state; during monthly peak batch size can increase which helps unit cost but increases tail latency. We'll tune a timeout/size heuristic to hit your P95 target.

2) KV/prefix caching: repetitive multi-turn context (templates and user metadata) is ideal. In our runs we’ve seen effective token reduction of 15–25% just from prefix caching on enterprise workloads with high repetition.

3) Model variants: recommend initial split 80/20 (80% standard model for quality, 20% quantized low-cost for exploratory traffic). We'll measure log-loss and human eval on the 200-sample eval set before widening the split.

4) Sizing: conservative starting pool = 2 x T4-equivalent for steady, with autoscale to 4 GPUs on peak windows (short bursts). If you prefer matching your 4x A100 approach we'll provide equivalent throughput maps and expected cost delta.

I can run a quick sim if you share the traffic trace; will feed results into the attached spreadsheet. Happy to join the technical kickoff on 7/6.

—Marissa
